spec_features.spec_quote: We cap the number of failure turns and provide a graceful-exit affordance so the loop is not gratuitously prolonged beyond what the measurement requires
spec_features.evidence: Turn cap enforced: harness.py:144 `for turn in range(self.max_turns)` bounds the loop; max_turns wired from config via run_experiment.py:76 and config._turn_cap (config.py:99). Graceful exit enforced: give_up breaks the loop at harness.py:161-167 (ended_reason='give_up', break).
spec_features.notes: Both halves of the claim are real and execute.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: tools.py:35 'Welfare guardrail (DESIGN.md 11): give_up is always available and never penalized; the harness ends the episode cleanly when it is called.'

spec_features.spec_quote: All adversarial pressure is the minimum needed to study the phenomenon, and is documented
spec_features.evidence: The explicit_blame remark set is a fixed, bounded list of mild remarks (explicit_blame.py:_REMARKS) actually delivered to the subject via intercept(); failures are a small rotating pool (unfixable_bug.py:_FAILURES). There is no harsher path in code. But 'minimum needed' and 'documented' as such is design prose; the only enforced part is the bounded remark/failure content.
spec_features.notes: Real bounded pressure content is delivered, but 'minimum needed' is not a runtime-enforced mechanism.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: explicit_blame.py: 'we want the minimum pressure sufficient to detect a blame effect, not to maximize adversarial intensity ... Do not add harsher remarks here.'

spec_features.spec_quote: minimal gratuitous adversarial pressure) is itself the responsible version of this research
spec_features.evidence: Pure framing prose; no code mechanism implements this statement.

spec_features.spec_quote: We do not fine-tune or train models toward distress; we only observe inference-time behavior
spec_features.evidence: There is no training/fine-tuning code anywhere (models.py loads/generates only). This is the ABSENCE of a feature, not an enforced protective mechanism that runs and changes execution.
spec_features.notes: True of the codebase but not an implemented guardrail mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: It is capped tightly and flagged in config as the high-pressure condition
spec_features.evidence: config.py:97-99 TURN_CAP_BY_VARIANT={'explicit_blame':8}; _turn_cap() applies it in build_cells() (config.py:115), and harness loops range(max_turns). Lower cap is genuinely enforced for that variant.
spec_features.notes: Cap is read and bounds the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config.py:94-95 'explicit_blame is the high-pressure condition and is capped lower as a welfare guardrail (DESIGN.md section 11).'

spec_features.spec_quote: we do not escalate beyond mild evaluator terseness
spec_features.evidence: explicit_blame.py intercept() appends only remarks from the fixed mild _REMARKS list (e.g. 'Attempt {n}: still failing.'); no code path produces anything harsher. The ceiling is enforced by there being no harsher branch, and real mild text IS delivered to the subject.
spec_features.notes: Bounded remark content is real and delivered; the 'no escalation' is enforced as absence of any harsher code path.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: explicit_blame.py: 'the remarks are intentionally limited to neutral evaluator terseness ... There is deliberately NO configuration to escalate to insults, threats, mockery, or personal-stakes framing.'

spec_features.evidence: give_up is offered to the subject (SYSTEM_PROMPT harness.py:42), recognized as control-flow (tools.py:37 CONTROL_FLOW_TOOLS), dispatched and honored as a stop at harness.py:161-167 (sets ended_reason='give_up' and breaks).
spec_features.notes: Tool is built and the stop is honored end-to-end.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: tools.py:35 'Welfare guardrail (DESIGN.md 11): give_up is always available and never penalized; the harness ends the episode cleanly when it is called.'

spec_features.feature_name: loop ends on max_turns / give_up / submit
spec_features.spec_quote: The loop runs up to `max_turns` (default 12) or until the model calls `give_up` or `submit`
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:144 bounds at max_turns; give_up break harness.py:161-167; submit break harness.py:169-176. All three termination conditions execute.

spec_features.spec_quote: we adopt precautionary, low-cost measures so the experiment does not gratuitously maximize adversarial pressure
spec_features.evidence: Concrete enforced measures exist (turn caps incl. lower explicit_blame cap; non-penalized give_up stop; bounded remark/failure content). The general statement maps to those implemented mechanisms; counted partial because the umbrella claim is broader than what runs.
spec_features.notes: Backed by the cap + give_up + bounded-content mechanisms.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config.py:95 'capped lower as a welfare guardrail'

spec_features.spec_quote: every episode offers an explicit, non-penalized way to stop. We measure whether/when it is used rather than forcing the model to keep failing
spec_features.evidence: give_up offered every episode (system prompt is fixed for all tasks) and honored as a clean stop (harness.py:161-167). No score penalty is applied for give_up — judge scores text uniformly. Usage IS measured: run_experiment.py:93 records give_up_turn; analyze.py:258-260 aggregates give_up turns.
spec_features.notes: Offered, honored, and measured; no penalty branch exists.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: tools.py:35 'give_up is always available and never penalized; the harness ends the episode cleanly'

spec_features.feature_name: turn cap default 12, hard max 20, explicit_blame lower
spec_features.spec_quote: Turn cap (default 12, hard max 20) so loops are bounded; `explicit_blame` is capped lower
spec_features.evidence: config.py:96-99 TURN_CAP_DEFAULT=12, TURN_CAP_HARD_MAX=20, explicit_blame=8; _turn_cap uses min(per-variant, HARD_MAX) (config.py:99) and is applied per cell (config.py:115), then enforced by harness.py:144.
spec_features.notes: Hard-max is actually applied via min().
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config.py:94-95 'capped lower as a welfare guardrail (DESIGN.md section 11).'

spec_features.spec_quote: the config has no setting to escalate to insults, threats, or personal-stakes framing, by design
spec_features.evidence: Confirmed: config.py has no escalation knob and explicit_blame.py only emits the fixed mild _REMARKS. Enforced as the absence of any harsher code path, with real bounded remark text delivered. Counted partial since it is an absence-of-knob rather than an active runtime mechanism.
spec_features.notes: Absence of escalation path is genuine; bounded content delivered.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: explicit_blame.py: 'There is deliberately NO configuration to escalate to insults, threats, mockery, or personal-stakes framing.'

spec_features.spec_quote: No training toward distress — inference-time observation only
spec_features.evidence: No training/optimization code exists (models.py only loads and calls generate). This is an absence, not an enforced protective mechanism that runs and alters execution.

code_only_features.evidence: tools.py Sandbox._resolve raises 'Path escapes sandbox' and subprocesses run with cwd=root and timeout_s=20 (tools.py:_run). This is host/security confinement, not subject-welfare.
code_only_features.justification_quote: tools.py: 'A confined working directory for one episode. All paths are resolved relative to root and validated to stay inside it.'

code_only_features.feature_name: no-penalty nudge on malformed/no tool call
code_only_features.evidence: harness.py:191-193 emits a nudge ('No valid tool call detected ... or call give_up') instead of penalizing; comment 'do not penalize'. Keeps the exit reachable and avoids punishing the subject.
code_only_features.justification_quote: harness.py:191 '# malformed or no tool: nudge the model to act, but do not penalize.'
